value.title: Pure Claude adapter and standard session output
value.summary: Explicit source loading -> pure Claude mapping -> common standard-first records -> OTLP JSONL, usable through SDK and CLI.
value.confidence: Product boundaries agreed; architecture/profile details and independent design review pending, no new feature proof yet.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Turn the configuration-only foundation into one useful collection path: enumerate/read explicitly supplied Claude Code JSONL files, map supplied native data without adapter I/O, and expose the same common records through an in-process Rust SDK and standard-first OTLP JSONL file/stdout output. A shared fakeable loader owns storage access; adapters remain deterministic units. Make ordinary new adapters cheap through stable contracts, a functional authoring example and shared conformance tests rather than runtime plugin machinery.

sections.name: goals
value: Read explicitly authorized Claude session inputs without coupling parsing to storage or output.
Provide deterministic independently unit-testable adapters and injectable storage/output ports.
Export useful standard-first records with native provenance and explicit limits rather than silently lose source facts.
Offer usable SDK and CLI paths plus a low-friction recipe for registering another adapter without editing core or existing adapters.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No access to real private transcripts during implementation or tests; all proof uses sanitized/synthetic fixtures and explicit temporary roots.
No daemon/watch service, remote OTLP transport, database, dynamic plugin loader, Flowspace indexing integration, pricing or live pij registry enrichment.
No universal conversation reconstruction, full-history branch/rewind materialization, automatic sidecar/attachment reads, or exactly-once delivery promise.
No SDK implicit HOME/environment source discovery; CLI requires explicit source scope.
No new independent canonical persisted telemetry encoding beside the standard-first OTLP JSONL profile.
No remote publication/main landing/global installation or workspace retirement without separate authorization.

value.claim: An application can inject a SessionLoader and choose a pure adapter without a filesystem or CLI dependency in the adapter; the same provided native data/state/options produces the same contracted result.

The shared file loader lists candidate sessions deterministically within an explicit source scope and reads bounded native batches; it neither interprets Claude content nor implicitly scans HOME or follows out-of-scope sidecars/symlinks.

Batch reads support explicit caller-owned resume positions, make progress across blank lines, retain incomplete final JSONL records without advancing beyond them, and report changed/truncated/replaced sources instead of silently losing data; unsupported source identity is named.

The Claude adapter maps user/assistant messages and supported text/reasoning/tool-call/tool-result parts, native identity/parent/session links, model and usage facts where present; repeated logical message IDs do not silently erase physical source records or fabricate a full inference operation.

Malformed or unsupported native records/parts, absent fields and source fragments have explicit diagnostics/provenance rather than panic, guessed values or an unqualified lossless/full-session claim; malformed bytes are not echoed in public errors.

The output writer emits valid UTF-8 OTLP LogsData JSONL with correct structured AnyValue/64-bit timestamp encoding and a documented standard-first semantic profile; native-only semantics use clearly named extensions, not invented standard attributes.

The SDK collection service composes loader, pure adapter and injected destination, returning a next checkpoint only after the batch is accepted by the output; output/read/map failures retain actionable error context without falsely advancing successful progress or claiming exactly-once writes.

Content collection/export is explicit: metadata-only is the conservative default and the caller/CLI can opt into message content; omitted/redacted/unsupported content is distinguished, and attachment references are never dereferenced implicitly.

The CLI can list explicit session inputs and export a selected Claude file to stdout or an explicitly selected file using the same SDK pipeline; machine diagnostics do not corrupt OTLP stdout and file creation does not silently overwrite existing data.

A second fixture adapter can be implemented and composed through the public contracts and one registration entry without modifying core or the Claude adapter; a concrete authoring example/template and common conformance suite document that path.

Existing configuration SDK/CLI behavior stays compatible, dependency checks reject I/O or outer-adapter dependencies in pure mapping/core surfaces, and all product tests are isolated from actual user stores and process-global environment mutation.

A fresh external Rust consumer and a temporary installed CLI execute equivalent fixture-backed collection/export with bounded batches and output error cases, documented usage/profile limits, and actual shared-loader/adapter/writer contract proof.

value.title: Read and export explicit Claude sessions through shared contracts
value.objective: Deliver one complete explicit Claude JSONL -> pure mapping -> typed/common OTLP output path with independently testable components and SDK/CLI parity.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Prior standard-first decision: ../archive/001-sdk-cli-foundation/assets/workshops/001-output-format.md; prior scratch reader experiments are inputs, not shipped proof. SessionLoader storage framing and pure native mapping are separate user-mandated boundaries. Native record/message/request identities differ; Claude sidecars can report parent sessionId; no data should be invented from missing fields. First-consumer Flowspace policies remain outside shared contracts.

value.approach: Fixture-driven unit and shared-contract tests for each pure/I/O boundary, then real temporary-file SDK/CLI end-to-end and external consumer proof.
value.rationale: Pure adapters are independently testable without mocks; loader/service/output failure and resume semantics need their own contract tests plus assembled proof.
value.focus_areas: No adapter I/O, bounded reads, partial tails, stale cursors, unknown records, multipart Claude messages, usage non-invention, OTLP encoding, explicit content opt-in, output failures, extension recipe, config regressions.
value.excluded: No live private stores, network services, exactly-once guarantee, broad native dialect coverage or unobserved platform claims.
value.mock_usage: Inject fake loader and output ports for orchestration; invoke pure adapters on bytes directly; use real tmp files and installed CLI for final integration.

value.location: docs/adapters.md, docs/telemetry-profile.md, SDK rustdoc and CLI/development usage sections.
value.rationale: Make the next ordinary adapter require only isolated mapping, fixtures/conformance and registration; document actual native coverage and output-profile semantics.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: Strict separation must be executable, not just a trait diagram. Claude physical JSONL records may be fragments/repeated IDs; OTLP standard fields must retain their real meanings. Session listing and raw batches need bounded resource behavior. Metadata-only default avoids accidental content export; explicit opt-in is documented and independently checked. Standard profile is source-derived logs, not a fake trace/inference model. No source is considered proven merely because prior scratch tests passed.
